correctness.rationale: Starting from the published two-site circle renewal expression, the Taylor coefficients are reconstructed exactly, with \(A_1=P_1/24\) and \(A_2=-P_2/720\). A direct identity eliminates p, yielding \(Q(b)=b^3+15b^2-16b+4\) and \(p=(5b-2)/(3b^3)\). Strict cubic root counts and physical probability signs give one admissible root; rational endpoints bracket it. The exact fourth quotient coefficient reduces at \(Q=0\) to \(H(b)/(5670b^8)\), with H positive throughout its certified rational interval. The nonzero Jacobian and analytic implicit-function argument prove the local square-root branch. All exact certificates and computations passed in verify.py; no numeric sampling was used to infer a general theorem.

originality.rationale: The same-model paper numerically reports the tricritical point and derivative conditions, but not the exact model-specific algebraic root, unique physical admissibility certificate, strictly positive cubic coefficient, or locally calibrated square-root onset. The earlier half-line model and general Landau theory do not state or directly supply this ring-specific exact invariant. Named published-finding corpus queries, literal term searches, source text and previously recorded scientific claims were compared; no covering statement was found. This is a qualified best-knowledge claim, not proof of exhaustive world uniqueness.
residual_risks: The September 2026 accepted journal page contains only abstract-level material; changes in a full accepted manuscript were not accessible in this comparison. The original May 2026 arXiv HTML detailed sections and Table 1 were inspected.
The semantic database and conventional search engines are not exhaustive, so unindexed technical appendices and alternative parameterizations may contain an equivalent algebraic characterization.

The local square-root exponent is a standard nondegenerate Landau mechanism; originality hinges on this model-specific exact coordinate, uniqueness, positivity and calibration, not claiming that exponent abstractly.

value.rationale: Exact identification and uniqueness of the physical tricritical control point, first positive nonlinear coefficient, and transverse local square-root calibration resolve a quantitatively relevant, previously numerical phase-diagram invariant. The result gives a falsifiable finite-parameter benchmark for this stochastic-search geometry and is not merely a finite numerical sample, standard normalization check or a generic Landau exponent relabeling.
